selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 5457, the Strengthening Agency Management and Oversight of Software Assets Act, requires federal agencies and Intelligence Community elements to conduct comprehensive assessments of their software inventories, usage, contracts, and costs. Based on these assessments, agencies must develop modernization plans to consolidate software entitlements, adopt cost-effective acquisition strategies, and require central CIO approval before subordinate components acquire software. The bill also directs the Office of Management and Budget, the General Services Administration, and the Government Accountability Office to oversee, recommend improvements for, and report on government-wide software management practices.

affected_groups.effect: Must conduct software assessments, develop modernization plans, establish central approval for software acquisitions, and submit reports to Congress and the OMB.
affected_groups.group: Federal Agencies and Intelligence Community Elements

affected_groups.effect: May be hired to support agency software assessments, provided they maintain operational independence and have no organizational conflicts of interest.

key_provisions: Requires federal agencies and Intelligence Community elements to complete a comprehensive assessment of their software inventory, contracts, additional fees, interoperability, and restrictions within 18 months of enactment.

Mandates that agency Chief Information Officers use assessment findings to create a plan to consolidate software entitlements, adopt cost-effective acquisition strategies, and restrict subordinate entities from acquiring software without approval.
Establishes detailed requirements for agency plans, including training employees on software negotiations, automating license management, and estimating costs and savings.

Requires the Office of Management and Budget, in coordination with the Administrator of General Services, to submit recommendations to Congress within two years to improve government software procurement policies.
Directs the Comptroller General (GAO) to submit a report to Congress within three years regarding government-wide software asset management trends, agency comparisons, and compliance.
Specifies that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out the act.
missing_information: Exact estimates of potential cost savings for the federal government.
Specific internal agency procedures for software approval beyond CIO sign-off.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 5457, the Strengthening Agency Management and Oversight of Software Assets Act, requires federal agencies and Intelligence Community elements to conduct comprehensive assessments of their software inventories, usage, contracts, and costs. Based on these assessments, agencies must develop modernization plans to consolidate software entitlements, adopt cost-effective acquisition strategies, and require central CIO approval before subordinate components acquire software. The bill also directs the Office of Management and Budget, the General Services Administration, and the Government Accountability Office to oversee, recommend improvements for, and report on government-wide software management practices.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts the internal management, procurement practices, and spending oversight of software assets across the entire federal government and the Intelligence Community. Its significance is evaluated as moderate because it changes administrative procedures and reporting requirements for federal technology assets without authorizing new funding.
